deficiencies.at_risk: Preschool children, adolescent girls, pregnant women, the very poor
deficiencies.effects: Kwashiorkor and marasmus in young children; underweight, stunting (low height for age) and wasting (low weight for height). In adults a sustained shortfall gives Chronic Energy Deficiency (BMI under 18.5).
deficiencies.foods: Pulses, milk and milk products, eggs, meat, fish, nuts and oilseeds, cereal-pulse combinations

deficiencies.at_risk: Women of reproductive age, pregnant women, infants and young children
deficiencies.effects: Anaemia — fatigue and breathlessness. In pregnancy it raises maternal mortality and the risk of low-birth-weight infants; in children it increases susceptibility to infection and impairs learning ability.
deficiencies.foods: Green leafy vegetables, legumes, dry fruits; meat, fish and poultry (better absorbed). Vitamin C-rich amla, guava and citrus improve absorption from plant foods; tea with meals blocks it.

deficiencies.at_risk: Populations in iodine-poor regions; pregnant women above all
deficiencies.effects: Goitre (enlarged thyroid); in the mother it causes cretinism, mental retardation, delayed motor development, stunting, deaf-mutism and neuromuscular disorders in the child.

deficiencies.at_risk: Preschool children, pregnant and lactating women
deficiencies.effects: Night blindness and Bitot's spots, progressing to xerophthalmia and irreversible blindness; also raises the risk of infection and death.
deficiencies.foods: Green leafy vegetables, carrot, pumpkin, mango, papaya; milk, egg, liver

deficiencies.at_risk: Pregnant women, especially preconception and the first trimester
deficiencies.effects: Macrocytic anaemia. In pregnancy, deficiency raises the risk of neural tube defects and other congenital anomalies and lowers birth weight.
deficiencies.foods: Green leafy vegetables, legumes, nuts, liver

deficiencies.at_risk: Diets without fresh fruit or vegetables; heavy smokers
deficiencies.effects: Weakness, bleeding gums and defective bone growth; poor wound healing and reduced iron absorption from plant foods.
deficiencies.foods: Amla, guava, citrus, tomato, capsicum, fresh vegetables

deficiencies.at_risk: Long-term vegetarians and vegans, older adults, people on metformin
deficiencies.effects: Megaloblastic anaemia with tingling and numbness, poor balance and, if prolonged, irreversible nerve damage. Often overlooked because folate can mask the anaemia while nerve damage continues.
deficiencies.foods: Milk and curd, paneer, eggs; fish and meat. Plant foods carry essentially none, so vegetarians rely on dairy or fortified foods.

deficiencies.at_risk: Little sunlight exposure, covered clothing, older adults, infants
deficiencies.effects: Softening and bowing of bones, delayed growth and bone pain in children; bone pain, muscle weakness and higher fracture risk in adults. Calcium cannot be absorbed properly without it.
deficiencies.foods: Sunlight is the main source; fortified milk, egg yolk, fatty fish

deficiencies.at_risk: Adolescents, pregnant and lactating women, postmenopausal women
deficiencies.condition: Osteopenia / osteoporosis; poor peak bone mass
deficiencies.effects: Reduced bone density and higher fracture risk; in children, inadequate peak bone mass. Works together with vitamin D.
deficiencies.foods: Milk, curd, paneer; ragi, sesame, green leafy vegetables, small fish eaten with bones

deficiencies.at_risk: Diets dominated by polished rice or refined flour; chronic alcohol use
deficiencies.effects: Wet beriberi affects the heart (oedema, breathlessness); dry beriberi affects the nerves (weakness, burning feet). Classically linked to polished-rice diets.
deficiencies.foods: Whole grains, millets, pulses, nuts; parboiled rather than polished rice

deficiencies.at_risk: Low intake of milk and green leafy vegetables
deficiencies.effects: Cracks at the corners of the mouth (angular stomatitis), sore red tongue, and a burning gritty sensation in the eyes.
deficiencies.foods: Milk and curd, eggs, green leafy vegetables, whole grains, pulses

deficiencies.at_risk: Diets dominated by maize/jowar with little pulse or milk
deficiencies.effects: The classic triad: dermatitis on sun-exposed skin, diarrhoea and dementia. Associated with maize-dominated diets.
deficiencies.foods: Groundnut, pulses, whole grains, milk, meat and fish

deficiencies.at_risk: Young children, adolescents, pregnant women, mainly-cereal diets
deficiencies.effects: Poor growth and delayed sexual maturation, more frequent and prolonged diarrhoea and respiratory infections, poor wound healing, loss of taste.
deficiencies.foods: Whole grains, pulses, nuts and oilseeds, milk; meat and shellfish

deficiencies.at_risk: Diets built on refined cereals with few vegetables, fruit or pulses
deficiencies.effects: Constipation and poor gut health; low intake is associated with higher risk of obesity, type-2 diabetes and heart disease.
deficiencies.foods: Whole grains and millets, pulses, vegetables, fruit with the skin on

rda.edition: ICMR 2010 RDA, as printed in the NIN Dietary Guidelines manual (2012)

reconciliation.why: The 2020 revision raised iron for adults, most sharply for women of reproductive age, on updated absorption and menstrual-loss estimates.
The 2020 revision raised adult calcium from 600 to 1000 mg/day.
The 2020 revision more than doubled the B12 allowance — relevant here, since a lacto-vegetarian diet gets B12 only from dairy.

rda.reconciliation_note: Menus are planned against the newer ICMR-NIN 2020 allowances, so the targets on Today and Analytics can read higher than this table for iron, calcium and B12. The table is reproduced as printed rather than quietly updated, because only some of its values changed in 2020 and the rest are unchanged.
rda.source: ICMR-NIN, *Dietary Guidelines for Indians — A Manual* (National Institute of Nutrition, Hyderabad; document dated 2012), Annexure 3, pp. 89-90. The allowances in that annexure are the ICMR 2010 revision.
rda.unit_note: Vitamin A, folate and vitamin B12 are micrograms (µg) per day. The source table's header prints 'mg' for these columns, but the values are µg — the µ glyph is lost in parts of the PDF. ICMR's vitamin A allowance is 600 µg retinol equivalent.
